VAL-SETUP-025.observed: Live: GET /operator/reservations/setup/locations/v17plv08r5v357bie335lyq8/conflicts without a token -> 401; with a setup token -> 200 {"locationId":"v17plv08r5v357bie335lyq8","conflicts":[]} (acme is currently conflict-free); ?date=2026-10-19 -> 200. GET .../validate and .../validation -> 200 {valid:true, issues:[turn_time_bucket_gap]}. Vitest: reservations-setup.test.ts 8/8 pass; the blocks test asserts GET /conflicts returns items with kind:'unassigned' and bookingId after the assigned tables are blocked. The endpoint runs the engine detectConflicts per upcoming business date and enriches each item with details.businessDate (rsv-setup-service.ts:1552-1592, 2435-2442).
VAL-SETUP-025.notes: Endpoint + Vitest verified. The App conflicts panel (/acme/reservations/settings) was NOT driven by me; browser groups own that check. Risk found by code inspection, flagged for browser confirmation: the panel expects SetupConflictDto {reservationId, confirmationCode, businessDate, partySize, reason} (apps/app/app/utils/reservations/setup-api.ts:124-141, apps/app/app/routes/_app+/$orgSlug_+/reservations+/settings._index.tsx:855-876) while the API returns engine items {kind, bookingId, tableId, details.businessDate}; fetchSetupConflicts raw-casts the response with no mapping, and the E2E spec stubs /conflicts with an empty list. A non-empty conflicts panel would therefore likely render blank date/reason fields. Not counted as a failure of the endpoint behavior I was assigned; needs browser validation.
